prerequisites: Having passed the subjects of Graphic Expression, Graphic Engineering and Informatics, as well as possessing basic knowledge and skills in the use of computer applications in the environments of the most widespread operating systems (Windows, Mac OS X, etc.), although at the moment, and for the programs to be used, only Windows versions have been developed.

learning_outcomes.text: To know and understand the fundamentals of 3D solid modeling from simple 2D geometries, as a means for the production and communication of ideas and projects.
To apply the geometric knowledge that underpins industrial design and computer-aided design.

To learn to express ideas, designs and projects graphically in a precise, clear and unambiguous way, as well as to acquire proficiency in solving graphic problems using sketching, drafting or CAD computer techniques.

To provide the student with resources for the generation of standardized technical representations using a 3D CAD system, while consolidating important concepts such as collaborative development, the possibilities of distributed computing, the use of repositories of reusable elements, etc.
To know and use a 3D CAD program, among the most commonly used, for the elaboration of technical engineering documents.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and concise presentation.
Ability to distribute resources and time and implement them in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability to work together and ability to develop multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to relate to other people and an open attitude towards creating new relationships.
Aptitude for professional insertion in diverse environments and with varied functions in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on the acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technology.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to existing work environments. Application configuration and customization.
Use of standardized templates for each work environment.
Visualization tools. Styles. Predefined 3D views. 3D rotation.
Generation of 3D parts. Introduction to 2D sketch tracing. Dimensional and geometric constraints. Work planes.
Generation of PARTS and hollows by projection, by revolution, between sections, by trajectory, and helical.
Modification operations of 3D geometries, pattern copy and generation of standardized holes. Virtual cuts. Parametrization of operations.
Generation of SHEET METAL parts. General sheet metal parameters. Special operations on sheet metal. Part development.

Generation of ASSEMBLIES. File management. Construction of assemblies from parts. Relationships between assembly parts. Use of pattern copies. Animation of disassembly and exploded views of assemblies.
Generation of 2D DRAWINGS from 3D. Format configuration. Part and assembly drawings.
Generation of lists, bill of materials and exploded views. Import and export with AutoCAD.

Other ADVANCED TOOLS. Generation of complex surfaces. Introduction to CAE analysis. Automatic generation of simple mechanical systems. Wiring design. Dashboard design. Animation and photorealistic rendering tools.
teaching_methods: Practical sessions in the computer lab (Labs)

assessment_methods.method: Practices carried out in different sessions
Participation in activities developed in class
Assignments proposed to be done in class or at home

assessment_rules: Throughout the course, in-class practices will be evaluated with a weighting of 30% of the total grade. The remaining 70% will be obtained from directed personal assignments and a final in-person exam, which will also be partially directed. The final exam of theoretical and practical knowledge will take place at the end of the semester after practical activities are concluded. Participation in class activities and proposed assignments will also be considered for evaluation.
